course.title: Ronin Trading System
course.subtitle: A coach-led structural momentum course for US stock swing trading, professional execution, and trader psychology.
course.disclaimer: Educational content only. No lesson, example, tool, or community discussion is financial advice, a signal, or a guarantee of results.

levels.title: Level 1 — Beginner Foundations
levels.description: Learn the system boundaries, market regimes, leadership, watchlists, relative strength, catalysts, and the mental discipline to wait.

levels.title: Level 2 — Intermediate Structure and Execution
levels.description: Master the two parent setups, key levels, volume, timeframe alignment, 30-minute triggers, and entry efficiency.

levels.title: Level 3 — Advanced Professional Execution
levels.description: Integrate risk, portfolio heat, trade management, psychology, journaling, review, and the complete playbooks.

levels.title: Member Resources
levels.description: Build the TradingView workspace and join the private Discord community after the core training.

modules.title: Orientation: The Ronin Framework
modules.description: Build the correct mental model for the course, understand the two parent setups, and learn the decision sequence before studying individual patterns.
objectives: Explain the boundaries of the Ronin Trading System and its two parent setups.
Use the complete decision sequence from market condition to post-trade review.
Study charts with a deliberate-practice process instead of memorizing isolated rules.
Adopt a professional mindset based on responsibility, uncertainty, and process.

lessons.title: Welcome to the Ronin Trading System
lessons.summary: The purpose of the system and the difference between prediction and preparation.

lessons.title: The Complete Decision Map
lessons.summary: A top-down map from market regime to post-trade review.

lessons.title: Responsibility, Uncertainty, and the Professional Mindset
lessons.summary: Build the mental foundation required to follow a rule-based system when outcomes remain uncertain.

lessons.title: How to Study and Build Pattern Recognition
lessons.summary: A practical study method for turning rules into visual skill.

modules.title: Market Conditions, Patience, and Exposure
modules.description: Learn when the environment supports long swing trades, how leaders provide market feedback, and why waiting is a professional action.
objectives: Classify the market as Aggressive, Constructive, Defensive, or No Trade.
Use the behavior of leading stocks as real-time evidence about market quality.
Build and update the Ronin Trend Map at the close and after the open.
Control overtrading by matching activity to opportunity rather than emotion.

lessons.title: The Four Ronin Market Regimes
lessons.summary: A practical regime model: Aggressive, Constructive, Defensive, and No Trade.

lessons.title: Let Leading Stocks Tell You the Truth
lessons.summary: Why the behavior of elite stocks often matters more than index headlines.

lessons.title: Patience and the Urge to Overtrade
lessons.summary: Recognize the emotional need for action and build rules that keep activity aligned with opportunity.

lessons.title: Build the Daily Trend Map
lessons.summary: A repeatable premarket and end-of-day process for classifying the environment.

modules.title: Stock Selection, Focus, and Watchlists
modules.description: Reduce thousands of stocks to a focused list of liquid leaders with sufficient movement, real catalysts, and clear structural potential.
objectives: Define a practical universe of liquid US-listed stocks with sufficient movement.
Separate genuine leaders from temporary momentum and weak rebounds.
Convert scanner output into weekly, developing, and actionable watchlists.
Protect attention from noise, novelty, and fear of missing out.

lessons.title: Define the Trading Universe
lessons.summary: Liquidity, price, movement, and why not every stock deserves attention.

lessons.title: Identify Genuine Market Leaders
lessons.summary: Price leadership, group leadership, and the difference between strength and temporary excitement.

lessons.title: Focus, FOMO, and Information Noise
lessons.summary: Protect attention, avoid novelty bias, and stop abandoning prepared watchlists for random movers.

lessons.title: Build Weekly and Daily Watchlists
lessons.summary: Turn scanner results into a small, prioritized list with preplanned levels.

modules.title: Relative Strength and Evidence-Based Thinking
modules.description: Use relative strength to identify leadership early while avoiding confirmation bias and attachment to a stock story.
objectives: Distinguish the RS line, RS Rating, and price leadership.
Recognize hidden strength when a stock resists broad-market weakness.
Apply a consistent RS checklist before studying an entry.
Use disconfirming evidence to prevent bias from replacing chart analysis.

lessons.title: RS Line, RS Rating, and Price Leadership
lessons.summary: Understand what each relative-strength tool measures and how they work together.

lessons.title: Read RS During Market Weakness
lessons.summary: How hidden leadership appears when indexes are under pressure.

lessons.title: Confirmation Bias and Story Attachment
lessons.summary: Use relative-strength evidence without searching only for reasons that support an existing opinion.

lessons.title: The Ronin RS Checklist
lessons.summary: Turn relative strength into a consistent pre-trade filter.

modules.title: Earnings Gaps, HVE, and Institutional Urgency
modules.description: Recognize meaningful institutional events, map their levels, and wait for constructive digestion instead of chasing expansion.
objectives: Identify the structural qualities of a meaningful earnings gap.
Use HVE and HV1 as evidence of urgency, not as automatic entry signals.
Evaluate post-event digestion and the first actionable continuation structure.
Control FOMO after large expansion days and wait for efficient structure.

lessons.title: Anatomy of a Quality Earnings Gap
lessons.summary: What makes an earnings gap structurally important rather than a one-day reaction.

lessons.title: HVE, HV1, and Institutional Urgency
lessons.summary: Use abnormal volume as context without turning it into a standalone signal.

lessons.title: Chasing Expansion and the Fear of Missing Out
lessons.summary: Stay disciplined after earnings gaps and high-volume moves by separating proof of demand from entry location.

lessons.title: Post-Event Digestion and the First Setup
lessons.summary: How to recognize when a high-volume event is being absorbed constructively.

lessons.title: Foundation Milestone: Market, Leaders, and Mindset
lessons.summary: Demonstrate mastery of the Beginner level before unlocking structure and execution.

modules.title: Flat Base Breakout
modules.description: Master the prior expansion, location, tightness, volume dry-up, pivot, confirmation, and failure conditions of the core breakout setup.
objectives: Recognize a valid flat base as contraction after proven strength.
Judge location, depth, tightness, and the quality of the final contraction.
Map a clear pivot and require meaningful confirmation through it.
Reject loose bases, repeated failures, and late entries.
Remain emotionally neutral when a breakout is missed or fails.

lessons.title: Anatomy of the Ronin Flat Base
lessons.summary: The prior move, location, depth, tightness, and final contraction.

lessons.title: Volume Dry-Up and the Breakout Pivot
lessons.summary: How declining supply and a clear upper boundary create the setup.

lessons.title: Breakout Confirmation and Entry Quality
lessons.summary: What a valid breakout should look like and why one cent above the pivot is not enough.

lessons.title: Breakout FOMO, Missed Trades, and Emotional Neutrality
lessons.summary: Handle anticipation, missed breakouts, and failed attempts without abandoning the flat-base rules.

lessons.title: Failed Breakouts and Base Disqualifiers
lessons.summary: Recognize when the structure is chop, distribution, or no longer actionable.

modules.title: Controlled Pullback
modules.description: Master first and later pullbacks in proven leaders, including 8 EMA, 21 EMA, prior-breakout, and weekly 8 EMA continuation structures.
objectives: Distinguish a low-supply pullback from technical deterioration.
Prioritize the first pullback after an earnings or institutional expansion.
Evaluate later pullbacks and weekly 8 EMA reactions with a higher standard.
Wait for the return of demand instead of buying a moving-average touch.
Manage fear and the need to call the exact bottom.

lessons.title: Anatomy of a Controlled Pullback
lessons.summary: The prior trend, quality of decline, support, and return of strength.

lessons.title: The First Pullback After an Earnings Gap
lessons.summary: Why the first continuation structure after institutional expansion receives priority.

lessons.title: Second Pullback and Weekly 8 EMA Rejection
lessons.summary: When a later pullback remains valid and why it requires stronger evidence.

lessons.title: Fear During Pullbacks and the Need to Be Right
lessons.summary: Read controlled weakness objectively without trying to catch the exact low or defend a prediction.

lessons.title: Pullback Failure and Deterioration
lessons.summary: Distinguish normal profit-taking from institutional selling.

modules.title: Key Levels and Structural Confluence
modules.description: Map important price levels before the stock reaches them and judge the reaction rather than predicting support.
objectives: Map prior pivots, earnings-gap levels, HVE lows, and major daily or weekly support.
Use confluence to improve location without cluttering the chart.
Separate a planned level from proof that buyers are defending it.
Avoid anchoring, hope, and moving levels after the trade begins.

lessons.title: How to Map Key Levels
lessons.summary: Prior pivots, gap levels, high-volume lows, and former resistance.

lessons.title: Confluence Without Clutter
lessons.summary: Combine horizontal structure, moving averages, and volume intelligently.

lessons.title: The Reaction Is the Signal
lessons.summary: Judge the stock by how it behaves at the level, not by the existence of the level.

modules.title: Volume Contraction and Expansion
modules.description: Read volume as evidence of participation and supply, then combine it with price instead of treating it as a standalone signal.
objectives: Interpret expansion volume, dry-up, relative volume, and abnormal selling.
Recognize genuine volume contraction inside bases and pullbacks.
Judge breakout and reversal volume in the context of price and time of day.
Avoid indicator fixation and confirmation bias.

lessons.title: The Language of Volume
lessons.summary: Interpret volume only in relation to price, location, and the stage of the pattern.

lessons.title: Recognize True Volume Dry-Up
lessons.summary: How declining activity reveals supply contraction inside bases and pullbacks.

lessons.title: Breakout Volume, Reversal Volume, and Failure
lessons.summary: What volume should do when the stock attempts to resume its trend.

modules.title: Weekly, Daily, and 30-Minute Structure
modules.description: Give each timeframe one job: weekly context, daily setup, and 30-minute execution.
objectives: Use the weekly chart to judge trend, maturity, and overhead supply.
Use the daily chart to define the setup, key level, and invalidation.
Use the 30-minute chart only to refine an already valid daily setup.
Prevent timeframe hopping when a trade becomes uncomfortable.

lessons.title: The Weekly Chart: Strategic Context
lessons.summary: Stage, overhead supply, weekly 8 EMA, and trend maturity.

lessons.title: The Daily Chart: Setup and Invalidation
lessons.summary: Classify the pattern, mark levels, and determine what must happen next.

lessons.title: Multi-Timeframe Alignment
lessons.summary: Combine strategic context, daily structure, and tactical timing without contradiction.

modules.title: 30-Minute Triggers and Entry Efficiency
modules.description: Use four repeatable intraday triggers, Low-of-Day ATR distance, structural stop distance, and a no-chase protocol.
objectives: Recognize the higher-low, reclaim, pivot-breakout, and opening-compression triggers.
Calculate Low-of-Day distance as a percentage of daily ATR.
Keep entry-to-stop distance generally within approximately one daily ATR.
Reject late entries even when the stock remains strong.
Control hesitation, impulse, and trigger-related FOMO.

lessons.title: The Four Primary 30-Minute Triggers
lessons.summary: Higher low, pivot breakout, reclaim, and opening-range compression.

lessons.title: Low-of-Day ATR Efficiency
lessons.summary: Measure whether the entry is still close enough to the day’s risk anchor.

lessons.title: Entry-to-Stop ATR and Structural Distance
lessons.summary: Prevent artificial stops and reject trades whose structure is too wide.

lessons.title: Hesitation, Impulse, and Trigger Discipline
lessons.summary: Execute a valid trigger without freezing, anticipating, or chasing after the planned entry is gone.

lessons.title: The No-Chase Protocol
lessons.summary: A decision tree for handling a stock that moves without you.

lessons.title: Structure Milestone: Setups, Volume, and Execution
lessons.summary: Demonstrate mastery of Flat Bases, Controlled Pullbacks, key levels, volume, timeframes, and entries.

modules.title: Risk, Position Sizing, and Drawdown Control
modules.description: Place structural stops, size positions mathematically, manage correlated exposure, and remain consistent through losses and drawdowns.
objectives: Place the stop where the trade thesis is structurally invalid.
Apply the 0.5% account-risk rule and 15% maximum-position rule correctly.
Measure portfolio heat and correlated exposure.
Follow a drawdown protocol instead of changing size emotionally.

lessons.title: Structural Stop Placement
lessons.summary: Place the stop where the setup is wrong, not at an arbitrary percentage.

lessons.title: Position Size Formula
lessons.summary: Calculate shares from account risk and apply the maximum allocation cap.

lessons.title: Handling Losses, Losing Streaks, and Drawdowns
lessons.summary: Use a written protocol to protect decision quality when recent results create fear, frustration, or urgency.

lessons.title: Portfolio Heat and Correlation
lessons.summary: Control the combined risk of several positions that may behave like one trade.

modules.title: Trade Management and Emotional Discipline
modules.description: Recognize failure quickly, allow healthy trends to work, trail structurally, and manage adds and trims without fear or greed.
objectives: Separate a thesis failure from normal price movement.
Manage a working position while its trend and structure remain healthy.
Trail stops using price structure and the appropriate moving average.
Add only after a new qualified structure and track maximum committed risk.
Avoid automatic breakeven stops, premature selling, and greed-driven holding.

lessons.title: When the Trade Is Not Working
lessons.summary: Recognize failed breakouts, failed reclaims, and loss of structure.

lessons.title: When the Trade Is Working
lessons.summary: Use structure, not the profit amount, to decide whether to remain.

lessons.title: Trailing the Trend
lessons.summary: Choose the trailing method that matches the speed and maturity of the stock.

lessons.title: Greed, Fear, Breakeven Stops, and the Disposition Effect
lessons.summary: Manage open profit and loss from structure rather than emotional comfort.

lessons.title: Adds, Trims, and Maximum Committed Risk
lessons.summary: Scale only when the stock creates new structure and track the real risk of the complete position.

modules.title: Journaling, Psychology, and Continuous Improvement
modules.description: Build an evidence-based review process that separates outcome from execution and turns emotional mistakes into specific rules.
objectives: Record the complete context, plan, execution, management, and result of each trade.
Grade process separately from profit and loss.
Track emotional states, triggers, and rule violations without excuses.
Use daily, weekly, and monthly reviews to improve one behavior at a time.
Apply a reset protocol after revenge impulses, losses, or emotional overload.

lessons.title: The Complete Trade Record
lessons.summary: What to record before, during, and after every position.

lessons.title: Separate Process From Outcome
lessons.summary: Why a winning violation is dangerous and a disciplined loss can be valuable.

lessons.title: Revenge Trading, Consistency, and the Reset Protocol
lessons.summary: Recognize emotional escalation early and return to the process before another trade is considered.

lessons.title: Daily, Weekly, and Monthly Review Cycle
lessons.summary: Turn individual trades into a reliable feedback loop.

modules.title: Integrated Playbooks and Final Certification
modules.description: Combine the entire system into two complete playbooks, a weekly and daily workflow, and a final mastery assessment.
objectives: Execute the Flat Base Breakout playbook from market context through review.
Execute the Controlled Pullback playbook from market context through review.
Follow the complete weekend, premarket, intraday, and end-of-day workflow.
Demonstrate technical and psychological mastery before increasing responsibility.

lessons.title: Flat Base Playbook
lessons.summary: The complete qualification, trigger, management, and rejection checklist.

lessons.title: Controlled Pullback Playbook
lessons.summary: The complete qualification, support, confirmation, and rejection checklist.

lessons.title: The Complete Weekly and Daily Workflow
lessons.summary: A repeatable operating routine from weekend scans to post-market review.

lessons.title: Final Ronin Checklist and Certification
lessons.summary: Demonstrate mastery of the framework before trading it with meaningful size.

lessons.title: Advanced Milestone: Final Ronin Mastery Assessment
lessons.summary: Prove that technical skill, risk discipline, and psychological control operate as one complete process.

modules.title: TradingView Workspace Setup
modules.description: Build the Ronin Full chart workspace, install the required indicators, and read the chart in a fixed order.
objectives: Install and configure the four required TradingView scripts.
Apply the complete Ronin Full color palette.
Build a clean weekly, daily, and 30-minute chart workflow.
Use indicators as measurements and context rather than decision substitutes.

lessons.title: Build the Ronin TradingView Workspace
lessons.summary: Create a clean chart where price, structure, volume, relative strength, and entry efficiency each have one clear job.

lessons.title: Install the Four Required Indicators
lessons.summary: Install the official scripts and understand why the system uses each one.

lessons.title: Apply the Ronin Full Color Palette
lessons.summary: Configure the exact parchment, candle, volume, moving-average, and markup colors used throughout the course.

lessons.title: Read the Complete Ronin Chart
lessons.summary: Combine the indicators into one repeatable weekly, daily, and 30-minute workflow without turning them into automatic signals.

modules.title: Premium Discord Community
modules.description: Connect to the private community and use it for study, feedback, and accountability without outsourcing decisions.
objectives: Connect the Ronin Charts account to Discord securely.
Use the community for chart study, course questions, and process review.
Post plans using the Ronin decision framework.
Avoid herd behavior, signals, and dependence on other members.

lessons.title: What the Ronin Discord Is For
lessons.summary: Understand the purpose, channels, standards, and behavior expected inside the premium community.

lessons.title: Connect Your Discord Account
lessons.summary: Authorize Discord securely, join the private server, receive the premium role, and solve common connection problems.

lessons.title: Use the Community Without Losing Independence
lessons.summary: A practical posting and review routine that uses feedback to improve skill rather than copy trades.
